sentences.text: As against the compensation of Rs.28,85,000/- claimed by the unfortunate parents and brother (respondents No. 1, 2 & 3 herein) of deceased - Vijay Thakur by filing claim application under Sections 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 for his death in the motor accident on 05.12.2012, the Tribunal awarded a total sum of Rs.8,04,000/- as compensation along with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of institution of the claim petition till realization.

3. The gist of the claim before the Claims Tribunal, in brief, was that the deceased Vijay Thakur by driving Motorcycle bearing Registration No. C.G.-07-AC- 2676 with two pillion riders (Kamlesh,
Radhe Sahu) was coming towards Shivpara Durg from Shivnath River.

On the way Res. No. 4 by driving the vehicle Tractor Bearing Registration No. - CG-07-N-3658 and Trolley No. - CG-07- NA-5325 rashly and negligently hit the Motorcycle from behind as a result of which Vijay Thakur,
Kamlesh Sinha, Radhe Sahu received grievous injuries and Vijay Thakur died due to injury sustained by him.

For the death of Vijay Thakur his parents and brother filed claim case under Section 166 of the M.V. Act. 1988, for compensation of Rs. 28,85,000/- against the Respondents No.
4, 5, 6, 7 and the appellant herein.

sentences.text:
Accordingly, the Claims Tribunal has awarded total compensation of Rs.8,04,000/-
in favour of the claimants and fastened the liability of 50%- 50% upon the Appellant-insurance company (insurer of trolly bearing registration no. CG 7 NA 5325) and Respondent no.5 (owner of tractor bearing registration no. CG 7 N 3658).
Hence this appeal.
5. Learned counsel appearing for the appellant submits that the tractor trolley cannot move on its own, hence the trolley owner and the insurance company are not responsible for the accident.
Hence, they are not liable to pay the compensation.

6. Learned Counsel appearing for Respondent No.7 supported the impugned award and submits that on the date of accident, offending vehicle (Tractor) was not insured, therefore, the Claims Tribunal has rightly exonerated Respondent No.7 and fastened the liability upon owner of the Tractor.
7. No one present on behalf of Respondents No.1 to 6.
8. I have heard learned counsel appearing for the parties and perused the record of the Tribunal including award impugned.

9. As regards the argument of learned Counsel appearing for the Appellant/insurance company that the tractor trolley cannot move on its own is concerned, the Claims Tribunal on a close scrutiny held that the principle was established that in cases of accidental death caused by a tractor-trolley, both the owners are considered equally liable (50% each), as the accident was caused by the use of both the tractor and the trolley, and the responsibility cannot be separated.

Since the tractor (engine)
involved in the accident was not insured on the date of the accident, the respondent No. 5, the owner of the vehicle (Tractor), is vicariously liable for the payment of compensation.
Similarly, the trolley attached to the tractor was insured with the Appellant- insurance company.
Therefore, the Appellant on behalf of respondent No. 6, the owner of the trolley, is vicariously liable for the payment of compensation.
Thus, the claimants are entitled to receive the compensation amount from the Appellant and respondent No. 5, jointly and severally.
However, the Appellant and respondent No. 5 Dahar Singh @ Dihar Singh are equally (50% each) liable for the payment of the awarded amount and interest.
10. Looking to the entire material available on record, it appears that the appellant/insurance company utterly failed to prove its case.
The conclusion of the Claims Tribunal is based on the proper appreciation of oral as well as documentary evidence which does not call for any interference.
11. Accordingly, the appeal of the appellant-insurance company is hereby dismissed affirming the judgment passed by the learned Claims Tribunal.
12. Record of the Claims Tribunal along with the copy of this judgment be sent forthwith.
